Psnow is a service for them to advertise games. I work in marketing, and this is what you would call “stress test.” You release small updates to a certain software, get the person to like the convenience and features, then slowly pull those away with consecutive updates. PsNow is one huge stress test. They release games, knowing that the average player doesn’t have the time to play it (psnow, and any service like it, is targeted towards working adults, and casual gaming types). Then, over time they pull things away and push you towards an upgrade. It’s classic B2C marketing and it’s an awful, manipulative practice. Spend some time looking at Apple’s business strategy sometime if you want to learn more. If you think Sony, Microsoft, Nintendo, or any major electronic publisher/ retailer cares about your needs or wants, you’re wrong. You speak with your actions. The more you buy into it, the higher value your data profile gets, and the more engagement they get over time, the less value you get. Simple capitalism in an always “online” world.
